title: Start from what the repository already has
prompt:
# Story 2: Start from what the repository already has

- **Story**: XXX-first-download
- **Created**: 2026-11-07
- **Status**: Draft
- **Demo**: connect to an empty repository and see the note about its first commit; connect to a repository with documents, on GitHub
  and on GitLab, and see them appear in the project, with a summary.

## Story

As a team member, I want that connecting to a repository brings in the documents that are already there (and prepares an empty
repository), so that I start from what my team has and never from a blank project.

## Acceptance tests

An empty repository

- [ ] **Given** a repository with no commit, **When** the user connects, **Then** BWYN makes its first commit on the base branch: an empty
  `README.md` in the folder, with the message "BWYN: first commit", and the connection goes on. If the provider refuses an empty file, the
  file holds the title line "# <repository name>".
- [ ] **Given** that, **Then** a note says "The repository was empty, so BWYN made its first commit: an empty README.md in <folder>/ on
  <branch>." and BWYN never reads that `README.md` as a document.

The one-time download

- [ ] **Given** a repository with files in the folder, **When** the user connects, **Then** everything in the folder that BWYN knows is
  downloaded once from the base branch: drivers, architecture, runways, principles, ADRs, architectural enablers, and stories with their
  diagrams, task lists and UI examples. Files outside the folder, and files BWYN does not know, are ignored.
- [ ] **Given** a document with the same identity already exists here (a driver with text, a principle, a story, an enabler, the
  architecture, a runway), **Then** it is left alone and is compared at the next sync.
- [ ] **Given** the practices (`practices.md`), **Then** they are not downloaded: they are fixed in BWYN.
- [ ] **Given** the download is over, **Then** a note says "Downloaded once from main when connecting: 3 drivers, the architecture, 2
  principles, 2 ADRs and 4 stories with 3 diagrams. Documents that already exist here were left alone, and the practices are fixed in
  BWYN, so they are not downloaded."
- [ ] **Given** nothing was brought in, **Then** the note says "There was nothing to download from main yet, or everything is already
  here."
- [ ] **Given** the provider could not list the whole repository, **Then** an amber line says "<Provider> could not list the whole
  repository, so some files may be missing. Sync a document to get it."
- [ ] **Given** a file that could not be understood (for example a story that is in two folders), **Then** a warning says so, and nothing is
  deleted.
- [ ] **Given** the files that came down, **Then** their versions are remembered as the last synchronised ones, so that the first Sync
  compares against them.

When the download fails

- [ ] **Given** the connection worked and the download failed, **Then** an error says "Connected, but what is in the repository could not
  be downloaded: <reason>", the card stays "Connected", and an amber box says "What is in main has not been downloaded into this project
  yet." with a button "Download from main" (it reads "Downloading..." while it works).
- [ ] **Given** the download was done once, **Then** it is not done again by itself. **Given** the page is reloaded, **Then** the box does not
  come back.

On GitLab

- [ ] **Given** a GitLab project, **Then** every test above holds, with "GitLab" in the place of "GitHub" (and "project" for
  "repository" where the screen says so).
- [ ] **Given** a GitLab project with more files than one page of answers holds, **Then** all of them are listed, and the list is never
  reported as cut.
- [ ] **Given** a project inside groups and subgroups, **Then** its files are found and downloaded.

## Business rules and constraints

- The download is **once**, when connecting, or by the button after a failure. After that, Sync moves changes (stories 3 to 6).
- It never overwrites what exists here. It never deletes anything.
- The first commit of an empty repository is the only time BWYN writes to the base branch directly. Everything else goes through a
  pull request (or merge request).
- The files come through the backend (`tree` and `blob`). The browser never has the key.

## Out of scope

- Sending and receiving after that (stories 3 to 6).
- Choosing what to download, and downloading again to replace what exists here (the "force pull" of a story is story 4).

## Tasks

- [ ] **Task 1. Start from a GitHub repository**
  - Describe `tree` (the files under a folder with their blob SHA, and whether the list is cut), `blob` (the text of one file by SHA) and
    `init` (the first commit) in the OpenAPI document.
  - Implement the three in the GitHub provider.
  - Move the one-time download (`importExisting`) to use them, with the "exists here, leave alone" rules per kind of document.
  - Show the first-commit note, the summary of what came down, the cut-list line and the warnings.
  - Add "Download from main" after a failure, and remember that the download was done.
  - Test with a fake GitHub server: an empty repository (and one that refuses an empty file), a repository with every kind of document,
    one with documents that exist here, and a cut list.
- [ ] **Task 2. Start from a GitLab project**
  - Implement the three calls in the GitLab provider: the first commit of an empty project, the list of files through all its pages, and a
    file by SHA.
  - Run the tests of Task 1 against a fake GitLab server, with the same cases, a project with many pages of files, and a subgroup.

tasks.text: Define `tree`, `blob`, and `init` operations in the OpenAPI document (ADR-0014), placing the controller in `bwyn-rest` and the port interfaces in `bwyn-core` (ADR-0017)

Implement the `init` operation in the GitHub outbound adapter (`bwyn-infrastructure`): commit an empty `README.md` (falling back to `# <repo name>` if the provider rejects an empty file) on the base branch with the message "BWYN: first commit" (ADR-0017)

Implement the `tree` operation in the GitHub outbound adapter: list all files under the configured folder from the base branch, returning each file's path and blob SHA and a flag indicating whether the list was truncated (ADR-0017)
Implement the `blob` operation in the GitHub outbound adapter: fetch the text of one file by its SHA (ADR-0017)

Implement the `importExisting` application service in `bwyn-application`: orchestrate `tree` + `blob` calls, apply the "exists here, leave alone" rule per document kind, skip `practices.md`, store downloaded versions as the last-synchronised baseline, and record that the download was completed (ADR-0017)

Implement the frontend ViewModel and UI feedback in the interface-adapter and UI layers: first-commit note, download summary note, cut-list amber line, per-file warnings, download-failure amber box with "Download from <branch>" button, and suppression of the box after a successful download (AE-0002, ADR-0007)

Write Jest unit tests for the download ViewModel covering: empty-repository note, full-download summary, nothing-to-download note, cut-list line, unrecognised-file warning, failure state with retry button, and post-success suppression (ADR-0005)

Write backend unit tests (`*Test.java`) for the `importExisting` application service covering: empty repository, repository with every document kind, documents that already exist, `practices.md` skipped, truncated list, and unrecognisable file (ADR-0009)

Write a GitHub integration test (`*IT.java`) against a fake GitHub server covering: empty repository (and provider-rejects-empty-file variant), repository with every document kind, documents that already exist, and a truncated file list (ADR-0012)

Implement the `init`, `tree`, and `blob` operations in the GitLab outbound adapter, handling pagination so the full file list is always returned regardless of page count, and supporting projects nested in groups and subgroups (ADR-0017)
Write a GitLab integration test (`*IT.java`) against a fake GitLab server covering: all cases from the GitHub test, a multi-page file list, and a subgroup-nested project (ADR-0012)
Verify the full build and test suite completes within the ten-minute budget (Practice: Ten-Minute Build)
